newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Four firms offer to support troubled Romanian bank.
newsitem.headline: Four firms offer to support troubled Romanian bank.

text.p: Troubled Romanian private bank Dacia Felix SA, awaiting a court ruling on its reorganisation or liquidation, has drawn four offers of support from foreign and domestic firms, judge Ioan Georgiu said.

Under the recovery programme, four companies offered to inject capital or grant credits to Dacia Felix, once a fast growing bank but struggling for one year with bad debts of some $200 million and a 642.2 billion lei 1995 loss.

Swiss-based Winlook Management Zurich financial group was planning a $200 million injection into Dacia Felix, while Virgin Islands-based ADS Tortoga had offered a $45 million credit, said Georgiu, appointed by courts to decide the fate of the bank, headquartered in the Transylvanian city of Cluj.
Two Romanian firms, Alfa Real Estate and Lucescu Group -- held by former national soccer team trainer Mircea Lucescu -- had both offered some $60 million in cash and credits.
Georgiu said British group Dacia Phoenix Holding had also offered an unspecified amount of credits to shore up the bank.
According to the law, the central bank, which happens to be Dacia's main creditor, has to clear all equity offers.
The court has two weeks to consider those offers and rule on the bank's recovery plan or liquidation.
Romania has 35 commercial banks, six of which are state-run. Rules issued this year allow courts to wind up banks, if recovery plans are rejected.
Dacia said companies led by Sever Muresan, a former Davis Cup tennis player who lives in France and the bank's former figurehead, owe it some $200 million.

On Tuesday parliament's upper Senate voted a bill to allow the central bank to give credits to Dacia Felix to help small depositors to recover their money. The lower Chamber of Deputies has yet to pass the bill.
